script.title: Rate limiter ka race fix

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Purane code mein get aur set alag alag the. Do requests ek saath aayi, toh dono ne same count padha.

pr.display: get + set alag alag 💀 race condition

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Matlab burst mein sau ki limit ke bawajood usse zyada requests nikal sakti thi.

pr.display: 100 ki limit, par burst mein zyada nikal gayi 😬

dialogue.speaker: paplu
dialogue.text: Ab incr use ho raha hai. Socho, do requests ek saath incr karein, toh kya hoga?

pr.display: ab INCR. do requests ek saath? 🤔

pause.prompt: Two requests call INCR on the same key at the same moment. What do they get back?

dialogue.speaker: paplu
dialogue.text: Ek ko ek milega, doosre ko do. Redis incr atomic hai, beech mein koi ghus nahi sakta.

pr.display: INCR atomic hai ✅ 1 aur 2, koi race nahi

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Ek baat: agar incr ke baad aur expire se pehle server crash ho gaya, toh key kabhi expire nahi hogi. Isse ek Lua script mein daal do.

pr.display: nit: INCR ke baad crash → key bina TTL ke 👀 Lua script mein daalo

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Approve, follow up ke saath. Counter ke kaam mein hamesha atomic operation use karo.

script.takeaway: For counters under concurrency, use an atomic operation like INCR instead of a separate read and write.

questions.prompt: Why could the old limiter let more than 100 requests through?
choices: Two requests could read the same count before either wrote
questions.explanation: A separate GET and SET is not atomic, so concurrent requests overwrite each other's count.
